name: Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Ghundar
nameAr: محمد بن جعفر الهذلي مولاهم البصري، أبو عبد الله، المعروف بغندر
diedNote: 193 or 194 AH (Taqrib); the Shamela record also gives 192

deathVariants.authority: as given on the Shamela record

taqrib.ar: ثقة صحيح الكتاب إلا أن فيه غفلة
taqrib.en: Reliable, with a sound written record, though there is some inattentiveness in him.

role: The most reliable transmitter from Shu'bah; Shu'bah's stepson

verdicts.ar: هو أحب إلي من عبد الرحمن في شعبة
verdicts.en: I prefer him to Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi in Shu'bah.

verdicts.ar: إذا اختلف الناس في حديث شعبة فكتاب غندر حكم بينهم
verdicts.en: When people differ over a hadith of Shu'bah, Ghundar's book is the judge between them.

verdicts.via: Abu Hatim, from Muhammad ibn Aban al-Balkhi
verdicts.en: Ghundar is firmer than I am in Shu'bah.

verdicts.ar: كان من أصح الناس كتابا، وأراد بعضهم أن يخطئه فلم يقدر عليه
verdicts.en: He had one of the soundest written records of anyone; some people tried to catch him in an error and could not.

verdicts.ar: يكتب حديثه عن غير شعبة ولا يحتج به
verdicts.en: His hadith from anyone other than Shu'bah is written down but not relied on as proof.

verdicts.ar: أحد الأثبات المتقنين من أصحاب شعبة اعتمده الأئمة كلهم … أخرج له البخاري عن شعبة كثيرا وأخرج له حديثا عن معمر وآخر عن عبد الله بن سعيد بن أبي هند توبع فيهما
verdicts.en: One of the firm and precise companions of Shu'bah, relied on by all the imams. Al-Bukhari records much from him from Shu'bah, and one hadith each from Ma'mar and from Abdullah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, both of which are corroborated.

dhahabi.ar: الحافظ. قال ابن معين: أراد بعضهم أن يخطئه فلم يقدر، وكان من أصح الناس كتابا، بقي يصوم يوما ويوما خمسين عاما
dhahabi.en: The hadith master. Ibn Ma'in: some tried to catch him in error and could not; his written record was among the soundest; he fasted on alternate days for fifty years.

flags.label: Relied on for Shu'bah specifically
flags.detail: Abu Hatim restricts proof-value to his hadith from Shu'bah. In both of his appearances here (al-Bukhari 3126 and the Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah routes of hadith 15) he transmits from Shu'bah, so the restriction does not bite.

bio: Shu'bah's stepson, a Basran cloth-dealer whose written copy of Shu'bah became the court of appeal when Shu'bah's students disagreed. Ibn Hajar calls him “the firmest of people in Shu'bah” and explains that al-Bukhari sometimes added Ghundar's longer route beside a shorter one for that reason. Named by his laqab in hadith 3126 and by his name, Muhammad ibn Ja'far, in Muslim.

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 9, letter mim (Wikisource)
